deductions.label: Room-rent and proportionate deduction
deductions.insurerReason: Room category exceeds eligibility. Proportionate deduction applied as per policy.
deductions.ourReading: Kamala's room cost ₹7,500 a day. Your limit is ₹5,000 a day. So the insurer paid only two-thirds of the room and of the doctor and nursing charges. That is ₹10,000 less for the room and ₹11,600 less for doctors and nurses. The maths matches your policy rule.

citations.quote: Room, boarding and nursing expenses are payable up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day for a normal room and up to 2% of the Sum Insured per day for ICU.
Where the room category exceeds eligibility, all associated medical expenses shall be payable in the same proportion as the eligible room rent bears to the actual room rent.

evidence: Final bill page 1: "Deluxe single – ₹7,500 per day × 4 days"
questions: Was a room within ₹5,000 a day free when Kamala was admitted? If not, get a written note from the hospital and ask the insurer to look again.

deductions.label: Non-payable consumables
deductions.insurerReason: Non-medical items not payable as per Annexure II.
deductions.ourReading: Gloves, PPE kit and admission kit cost ₹6,900 (bill page 4). Your policy never pays for these items, and you don't have the extra cover that would. So this cut follows your policy.

citations.quote: List I – Items for which coverage is not available: gloves, PPE kit, admission kit, ...

evidence: Final bill page 4: "Gloves, PPE kit, admission kit – ₹6,900"
questions: Check that no medicine was wrongly counted as gloves or kits.

deductions.label: Other deductions (no reason given)
deductions.insurerReason: "Other deductions" – no reason or clause stated.
deductions.ourReading: The insurer's letter cuts ₹9,500 but gives no reason. We found nothing in your bill or policy that explains it. Ask the insurer to list what it is for.
evidence: Insurer's payment letter, page 2: "Other deductions – ₹9,500" with no reason
questions: Which items on the bill make up the ₹9,500?
Which rule in my policy allows this cut?
